source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Parathormone raises serum calcium mainly by:
questions.rationale: PTH releases calcium from bone; it raises calcium and lowers phosphorus (inverse relationship).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Parathyroid glands (PDF p. 255)
questions.quote: PTH elevates serum calcium levels by withdrawal of calcium from the bones.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which test best reflects average blood glucose over the past 3 months?
questions.rationale: HbA1c reflects glucose levels over the RBC lifespan, about 3–4 months.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Diagnostic tests for DM (PDF p. 256)
questions.quote: Reflects serum glucose levels for the past 3 — 4 mos.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: On a thyroid scan, a 'cold' nodule is more likely to be:
questions.rationale: Nonfunctioning (cold) nodules are more suspicious for cancer; hot nodules are usually benign.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroid scan (PDF p. 257)
questions.quote: May differentiate benign (hot) and malignant (cold) thyroid tumors.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a 24-hour urine VMA test for pheochromocytoma, the client avoids:
questions.rationale: Coffee, tea, chocolate, bananas, vanilla and aspirin can alter VMA results.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 VMA test (PDF p. 258)
questions.quote: o Coffee o Chocolate o Tea o Bananas o Vanilla o Aspirin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An adult with enlarging hands, feet and jaw most likely has excess:
questions.rationale: GH excess after epiphyseal closure causes acromegaly; before closure, gigantism.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Growth hormone disorders (PDF p. 259)
questions.quote: Acromegaly. Is hypersecretion of GH in adults (after epiphyseal closure).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A head-injury client has low serum sodium, weight gain and concentrated urine. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: SIADH: excess ADH retains water, causing dilutional hyponatremia and concentrated urine.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 SIADH (PDF p. 260)
questions.quote: SIADH is characterized by excessive retention of water by the renal tubules, low serum sodium (dilutional hyponatremia)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The priority nursing measure for SIADH is:
questions.rationale: Restrict fluids, monitor weight and sodium, and give prescribed diuretics or demeclocycline.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 SIADH management (PDF p. 260)
questions.quote: Restrict fluid intake as prescribed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client passes large volumes of very dilute urine with low specific gravity. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: DI (low ADH) causes polyuria up to 20 L/day, dilute urine, polydipsia and dehydration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Diabetes insipidus (PDF p. 261)
questions.quote: The most characteristic manifestation Of D.I. is polyuria

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During a water deprivation test, the client's urine stays dilute despite withholding fluids. This confirms:
questions.rationale: In DI, withholding fluids for 4–18 hours fails to concentrate the urine because ADH is lacking.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Diabetes insipidus (PDF p. 261)
questions.quote: If there is no increase in urine concentration, this confirms presence of D.I.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, why is the head of the bed kept elevated?
questions.rationale: Elevating the head promotes venous drainage and drainage from the surgical site; keep nasal packing and avoid nose blowing.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hypophysectomy (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: Keep head of bed elevated, at least for 2 weeks. To promote venous drainage and drainage from the surgical site.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After hypophysectomy, which client teaching is correct?
questions.rationale: Avoid nose blowing, coughing and bending (raise ICP and strain the site); keep HOB elevated; use soft oral care.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hypophysectomy (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: Instruct client to avoid blowing the nose and activities that increase intracranial pressure (ICP).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A woman fails to lactate and has fatigue and low BP after a severe postpartum hemorrhage. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Sheehan's syndrome is pituitary necrosis from severe postpartum bleeding and hypotension.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Sheehan's syndrome (PDF p. 266)
questions.quote: Is hypopituitarism caused by postpartum pituitary necrosis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which set of findings suggests hyperthyroidism?
questions.rationale: Hyperthyroidism: everything high, fast and wet—tachycardia, tremor, weight loss, heat intolerance, diarrhea.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hyperthyroidism (PDF p. 267)
questions.quote: Heat intolerance

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Graves' exophthalmos should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Protect exposed eyes with artificial tears and dark glasses to prevent corneal ulceration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hyperthyroidism management (PDF p. 269)
questions.quote: Instill artificial tears at regular intervals. Advise patient to wear dark sunglasses when going out under the sun

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on methimazole develops fever and sore throat. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Thioamides (methimazole, PTU) can cause agranulocytosis; sore throat and fever must be reported.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Antithyroid medications (PDF p. 269)
questions.quote: Side effects: Agranulocytosis (Neutropenia) with leukopenia (fever, sore throat, skin rash, diarrhea).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Lugol's solution is given before thyroidectomy to:
questions.rationale: Iodine shrinks the gland and reduces vascularity, lowering bleeding and thyroid storm risk; give via straw diluted in juice.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroidectomy preop (PDF p. 270)
questions.quote: To reduce the size and vascularity of the thyroid gland and prevent postop hemorrhage and thyroid crisis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After thyroidectomy, which item must be at the bedside?
questions.rationale: Bleeding, edema or hypocalcemic laryngospasm can obstruct the airway; keep trach set, oxygen and suction ready.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroidectomy postop (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Ilave tracheostomy set, oxygen and suction available at the bedside.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After thyroidectomy, the nurse checks the dressing at the back of the neck because:
questions.rationale: Blood drains by gravity to the back of the neck; check posteriorly and watch for respiratory distress.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroidectomy postop (PDF p. 270)
questions.quote: Check dressing anteriorly and at the back of the neck.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After thyroidectomy, a client has tingling lips and a positive Trousseau's sign. The nurse prepares:
questions.rationale: Damage to the parathyroids causes hypocalcemia and tetany; keep calcium gluconate ready.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroidectomy postop (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Keep Calcium gluconate readily available, for tetany.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Severe, increasing hoarseness after thyroidectomy suggests:
questions.rationale: Mild hoarseness is normal; severe hoarseness, stridor or dysphonia suggests laryngeal nerve injury.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroidectomy postop (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Severe hoarseness indicates laryngeal nerve damage.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client in thyroid storm has a temperature of 40 °C. Which antipyretic is preferred?
questions.rationale: Aspirin increases free thyroid hormone; use acetaminophen and cooling measures.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroid storm (PDF p. 272)
questions.quote: Avoid ASA. Salicylates increase free thyroid hormone levels.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which set of findings suggests hypothyroidism?
questions.rationale: Hypothyroidism: everything low, slow and dry—bradycardia, lethargy, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hypothyroidism (PDF p. 273)
questions.quote: Cold intolerance; subnormal body temperature.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Clients with hypothyroidism are more sensitive to which drugs?
questions.rationale: Slow metabolism increases sensitivity to sedatives, narcotics and anesthetics; these can precipitate myxedema coma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hypothyroidism (PDF p. 274)
questions.quote: Increased sensitivity to sedatives, narcotic and anesthetics.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should levothyroxine be taken?
questions.rationale: Take in the morning without food; separate by 4 hours from iron, antacids, multivitamins and sucralfate.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroid replacement (PDF p. 275)
questions.quote: Instrtlct client to take the medication in the morning without food.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client starting levothyroxine reports palpitations and chest pain. The nurse recognizes:
questions.rationale: Report hyperthyroid signs (tachycardia, chest pain, palpitations, sweating); doses are started low and increased slowly.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Thyroid replacement (PDF p. 275)
questions.quote: Advise client to report signs of hyperthyroidism like tachycardia, chest pain, palpitations and excessive sweating.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A hypothyroid client becomes hypothermic, bradycardic and stuporous after surgery and sedation. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Myxedema coma: profound depression of vital signs (hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension, hypoventilation); fatal if untreated.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Myxedema coma (PDF p. 275)
questions.quote: In myxedemic coma, all vital signs are profoundly depressed. It is potentially fatal.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet is appropriate for hypoparathyroidism?
questions.rationale: Hypoparathyroidism causes low calcium and high phosphorus; give calcium, vitamin D and phosphate binders.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 279)
questions.quote: Diet: High-calcium. low-phosphorous diet.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should alendronate be taken?
questions.rationale: Swallow whole with water on an empty stomach and stay upright 30 minutes to prevent esophagitis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Calcium regulators (PDF p. 279)
questions.quote: These should be taken with water at least 30 minutes before breakfast and to remain upright for at least 30 minutes.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with hyperparathyroidism should be encouraged to:
questions.rationale: High calcium causes polyuria and kidney stones; fluids prevent dehydration and stones. Move gently—bones are fragile.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hyperparathyroidism (PDF p. 280)
questions.quote: Increase fluid intake. To prevent dehydration and renal stone formation.
